High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: IA No. 22745 of 2023, an application under Section 301(2) of CrPC moved on behalf of complainant seeking permission of this Court to assist prosecution in the matter is taken up, considered and allowed for the reasons mentioned therein.
Shri Aditya Sharma, learned Counsel appearing for complainant is permitted to assist prosecution in the matter.

The present first bail application has been filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.287 of 2023 registered at Police Station- Lahar, District Bhind (M.P.) for offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) & 506 IPC.

As per the case of prosecution, victim, aged around 32 years, submitted a written complaint on 09-11-2023 with SHO, PS Lahar, District Bhind that she is married and has two children. entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accused Anup Dixit committed rape on her and threatened to kill her if she informs anybody about the incident.
Due to fear, she did not inform anybody.
Thereafter, she along with her husband and children shifted to Narsapur, District Medak, Sikandrabad.
Accused Anup came to Narsapur and requested her husband for a place to reside.
Her husband permitted him to live with him.
Anup Dixit used to commit rape on her under threat to kill her children.
Her husband returned to Lahar but she stayed at Hyderabad for studies of her children.
Anup Dixit used to commit rape on her at Naraspur.
She missed her menstrual cycle.
Thereafter, Anup Dixit left her home.
She came to Lahar and narrated the incident to her husband and mother-in-law.
When she complained to father of Anup Dixit, he threatened to kill her if she reports against Anup Dixit.
On such allegations, PS Lahar, District Bhind registered FIR at Crime No.287 of 2023 for offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 506 of IPC against applicant Anup Dixit and Pramod Dixit.
Statements of victim have been recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of CrPC.
Medico-legal examination of the victim has been conducted.
Investigation is underway.

Learned counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that as per allegations contained in the complaint and statements of victim, it is a case of consensual relationship between two persons.
No case of rape is made out against the applicant.
Applicant has been falsely implicated in the matter.
Applicant is a driver by profession and sole bread earner of the family.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving behind his family and home.
No custodial interrogation of applicant is required in the matter.
No criminal antecedent of similar nature is reported against him.
Applicant is ready to co-operate in the investigation.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of anticipatory bail.
Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence and prays for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary and documents.

Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Thus, the application is allowed.
